### Changelog generation has never been so easy

**Fully automated changelog generation** - This gem generates a changelog file based on **tags**, **issues** and merged **pull requests** (and splits them into separate lists according to labels) from :octocat: GitHub.

Since you don't have to fill your `CHANGELOG.md` manually now: just run the script, relax and take a cup of :coffee: before your next release! :tada:

### *What’s the point of a changelog?*

To make it easier for users and contributors to see precisely what notable changes have been made between each release (or version) of the project.

### *Why should I care?*

Because software tools are for _people_. "Changelogs make it easier for users and
contributors to see precisely what notable changes have been made between each
release (or version) of the project."

:arrow_right: *[https://keepachangelog.com](https://keepachangelog.com)*

## Installation

GitHub Changelog Generator is a [Ruby](https://www.ruby-lang.org/)
program, distributed as a RubyGem. The Ruby language homepage has an [Installation page](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/documentation/installation/).

Install the gem like:

    $ gem install github_changelog_generator

Depending on your system, you _may_ need to run the shell as an Administrator (Windows),
or use `sudo gem install github_changelog_generator` (Linux).


## Usage


### Running with CLI:

	   github_changelog_generator -u github_project_namespace -p github_project

(where the project namespace is _likely_ your username if it's a project you own, but it could also be the namespace of the project)


### Running with Docker

Using [Docker](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop) is an alternative to installing Ruby and the gem.

Example invocation:

    $ docker run -it --rm -v "$(pwd)":/usr/local/src/your-app githubchangeloggenerator/github-changelog-generator



- For GitHub Enterprise repos, specify *both* `--github-site` and `--github-api` options:

       $ github_changelog_generator --github-site="https://github.yoursite.com" \
                                  --github-api="https://github.yoursite.com/api/v3/"


This generates a `CHANGELOG.md`, with pretty Markdown formatting.

  #   future-release=5.0.0
  #   # Ruby-style comments, too
  #   since-tag=1.0.0
  #
  # The configuration format is <tt>some-key=value</tt> or <tt>some_key=value</tt>.
  #
  class ParserFile
    # @param options [Hash] options to be configured from file contents
    # @param io [nil, IO] configuration file handle
    def initialize(options, io = nil)
      @options = options
      @io = io
    end

    # Sets options using configuration file content
    def parse!
      return unless @io

      @io.each_with_index { |line, i| parse_line!(line, i + 1) }
      @io.close
    end

    private

    def parse_line!(line, line_number)
      return if non_configuration_line?(line)

      option_name, value = extract_pair(line)
      @options[option_key_for(option_name)] = convert_value(value, option_name)
    rescue StandardError
      raise ParserError, "Failed on line ##{line_number}: \"#{line.gsub(/[\n\r]+/, '')}\""
    end

    # Returns true if the line starts with a pound sign or a semi-colon.
    def non_configuration_line?(line)
      line =~ /^[\#;]/ || line =~ /^\s+$/
    end

    # Returns a the option name as a symbol and its string value sans newlines.
    #
    # @param line [String] unparsed line from config file
    # @return [Array<Symbol, String>]
    def extract_pair(line)
      key, value = line.split("=", 2)
      [key.tr("-", "_").to_sym, value.gsub(/[\n\r]+/, "")]
    end

    KNOWN_ARRAY_KEYS = %i[exclude_labels include_labels
                          summary_labels breaking_labels enhancement_labels bug_labels
                          deprecated_labels removed_labels security_labels
                          issue_line_labels between_tags exclude_tags]
    KNOWN_INTEGER_KEYS = [:max_issues]

    def convert_value(value, option_name)
      if KNOWN_ARRAY_KEYS.include?(option_name)
        value.split(",")
      elsif KNOWN_INTEGER_KEYS.include?(option_name)
        value.to_i
      elsif value =~ /^(true|t|yes|y|1)$/i
        true
      elsif value =~ /^(false|f|no|n|0)$/i
        false
      else
        value
      end
    end

    IRREGULAR_OPTIONS = {
      bugs_label: :bug_prefix,
      enhancement_label: :enhancement_prefix,
      issues_label: :issue_prefix,
      header_label: :header,
      front_matter: :frontmatter,
      pr_label: :merge_prefix,
      breaking_label: :breaking_prefix,
      issues_wo_labels: :add_issues_wo_labels,
      pr_wo_labels: :add_pr_wo_labels,
      pull_requests: :pulls,
      filter_by_milestone: :filter_issues_by_milestone,
      github_api: :github_endpoint
    }

    def option_key_for(option_name)
      IRREGULAR_OPTIONS.fetch(option_name) { option_name }
    end
  end
end

This directory contains a comprehensive configuration example for the **github-changelog-generator** tool, demonstrating the full range of available customization options.

- **`CHANGELOG.md`** - Sample output showing what the generated changelog looks like
- **`README.md`** - This documentation file

## Configuration File Overview

The `.github_changelog_generator` file uses a simple `key=value` format and supports comments with `#` or `;`.

### Basic Syntax

```
# This is a comment
option-name=value
option_name=value  # Both dashes and underscores work
```

## Configuration Sections

### 1. Project Settings

Essential settings that identify your GitHub repository:

```
user=github-changelog-generator
project=github-changelog-generator
```

- **`user`** - GitHub username or organization name
- **`project`** - Repository name

### 2. Version Range Settings

Control which versions are included in the changelog:

```
since-tag=1.0.0
due-tag=2.0.0
future-release=3.0.0
unreleased=true
unreleased-label=🚀 Upcoming Release
```

- **`since-tag`** - Generate changelog starting from this tag
- **`due-tag`** - Generate changelog up to this tag (optional)
- **`future-release`** - Version name for the next release
- **`unreleased`** - Include unreleased changes (`true` or `false`)
- **`unreleased-label`** - Custom label for the unreleased section

### 3. Label Configuration

Define which labels categorize issues and pull requests:

```
enhancement-labels=enhancement,feature,Feature Request
bug-labels=bug,fix,Bug Fix
breaking-labels=breaking-change,breaking
deprecated-labels=deprecated,Deprecated
removed-labels=removed,Removed
security-labels=security,Security,vulnerability
summary-labels=release-summary,Summary
exclude-labels=duplicate,wontfix,invalid,question
```

- **`enhancement-labels`** - Features and improvements
- **`bug-labels`** - Bug fixes
- **`breaking-labels`** - Breaking changes
- **`deprecated-labels`** - Deprecated features
- **`removed-labels`** - Removed features
- **`security-labels`** - Security fixes
- **`summary-labels`** - Release summaries
- **`exclude-labels`** - Issues/PRs to exclude from changelog

**Note:** Multiple labels are comma-separated, no spaces.

### 4. Section Customization

Customize the headers for each section in the changelog:

```
breaking-prefix=⚠️ **BREAKING CHANGES:**
enhancement-label=✨ **New Features & Enhancements:**
bugs-label=🐛 **Bug Fixes:**
deprecated-prefix=⚠️ **Deprecated:**
removed-prefix=🗑️ **Removed:**
security-prefix=🔒 **Security Fixes:**
pr-label=🔀 **Merged Pull Requests:**
issues-label=📋 **Closed Issues:**
```

- **`enhancement-label`** - Enhancements section header (note: use `enhancement-label`, not `enhancement-prefix`)
- **`bugs-label`** - Bug fixes section header (note: use `bugs-label`, not `bug-prefix`)
- **`deprecated-prefix`** - Deprecated features section header
- **`removed-prefix`** - Removed features section header
- **`security-prefix`** - Security fixes section header
- **`pr-label`** - Pull requests section header
- **`issues-label`** - Issues section header

```

base=HISTORY.md
header=# 📜 Changelog\n\nAll notable changes...
date-format=%Y-%m-%d
```

- **`output`** - Output filename (default: `CHANGELOG.md`)
- **`base`** - Base file to append generated changelog to (for migrating from manual changelog)

```
pull-requests=true
```

- **`issues`** - Include closed issues

```
author=true
compare-link=true
simple-list=false
verbose=true
```

```
github-api=https://github.yourcompany.com/api/v3/
```

- **`github-site`** - GitHub Enterprise site URL
- **`github-api`** - GitHub Enterprise API endpoint

Performance and network options:

```
http-cache=true
ssl-ca-file=/path/to/ca-bundle.crt
```

- **`http-cache`** - Enable HTTP caching for faster repeated runs
- **`ssl-ca-file`** - Custom SSL certificate bundle path

### Generate Changelog with This Configuration

```bash
cd examples/advanced_config
github_changelog_generator
```

The tool will automatically read the `.github_changelog_generator` file in the current directory.

### Use Configuration from Different Location

```bash
github_changelog_generator --config /path/to/.github_changelog_generator
```

### Override Configuration Options

Command-line arguments take precedence over configuration file:

```bash
github_changelog_generator --since-tag 2.0.0 --future-release 4.0.0
```

### Validate Configuration

Test your configuration without generating the full changelog:

```bash
github_changelog_generator --help
```

## Best Practices

### 1. Label Organization

Create a consistent labeling strategy in your GitHub repository:

```
# In GitHub, create these labels:
enhancement → #a2eeef
bug → #d73a4a
breaking-change → #e99695
security → #d93f0b
documentation → #0075ca
```

### 2. Exclude Noise

Use `exclude-labels` to filter out meta issues:

```
exclude-labels=duplicate,wontfix,invalid,question,wip,work-in-progress
```

### 3. Version Management

Use meaningful version tags and milestones:

- Tag releases: `v1.0.0`, `v1.1.0`, `v2.0.0`
- Create milestones matching tag names
- Assign issues to milestones when fixed

### 4. Release Summaries

Add release summaries for major versions:

1. Create a GitHub issue with the `release-summary` label
2. Write your release notes in the issue description
3. Add the issue to the version's milestone
4. Close the issue

### 5. Breaking Changes

Always label breaking changes appropriately:

- Use labels like `breaking-change` or `backwards-incompatible`
- Document what changed and migration steps in the issue/PR description
- Consider using a `BREAKING:` prefix in commit messages

### 6. Security Fixes

Handle security updates with care:

- Use `security` label for all security-related issues
- Follow responsible disclosure practices
- Document CVE numbers when applicable

## Troubleshooting

### Configuration File Not Found

Make sure the file is named exactly `.github_changelog_generator` (with the leading dot) and is in the current directory or specified with `--config`.

### Invalid Configuration Format

The configuration format is strict:

- ✅ `option-name=value` (correct)
- ❌ `option-name: value` (wrong - colon not supported)
- ✅ `# comment` or `; comment` (correct)
- ✅ `option-name=value1,value2,value3` (correct for arrays)

### GitHub API Rate Limiting

If you see rate limiting errors:

1. Generate a GitHub personal access token
2. Set environment variable: `export CHANGELOG_GITHUB_TOKEN=your-token`
3. Or use command line: `--token your-token`

### Empty Sections

If some sections don't appear:

- Check that issues/PRs have the correct labels
- Verify `exclude-labels` isn't filtering them out
- Ensure issues are closed and PRs are merged
- Check version range with `since-tag` and `due-tag`

You can create custom sections beyond the built-in ones. While not shown in this basic example, you can use label mapping to create entirely custom categories.

### Frontmatter for Jekyll/Hugo

Add YAML frontmatter for static site generators:

```
header=---\nlayout: changelog\ntitle: Changelog\n---\n# Changelog
```

### Integration with CI/CD

Automate changelog generation in your pipeline:

```bash
# .github/workflows/release.yml
- name: Generate Changelog
  run: |
    gem install github_changelog_generator
    github_changelog_generator --token ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

### Multiple Changelogs

Generate different changelogs for different audiences:

```bash
# Public changelog (exclude internal labels)
github_changelog_generator --exclude-labels internal,wip

# Detailed changelog for developers
github_changelog_generator --output CHANGELOG-DETAILED.md
```

- [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/)

This example configuration is provided as-is for demonstration purposes. The github-changelog-generator tool is licensed under the MIT License.
